stops.title: Carbohydrates: Glucose, Fructose & Disaccharides
stops.inShort: Glucose preparation from sucrose: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O --(H⁺)--> C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (fructose). Sucrose has α,β-1,2-glycosidic linkage; Maltose has α-1,4; Lactose has β-1,4-glycosidic linkage.

stops.title: Proteins, Peptide bond, Enzymes & Nucleic acids
stops.inShort: Peptide bond (−CO−NH−) links two α-amino acids with loss of H₂O. Proteins: Fibrous (keratin, myosin) and Globular (insulin, albumin). Enzymes are biological catalysts (globular proteins). DNA has A-T, G-C base pairs.

board.text: Write preparation of glucose from sucrose.
board.answer:
When sucrose (cane sugar) is boiled with dilute HCl or H₂SO₄ in alcoholic solution for about two hours, it hydrolyses to give equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose.
C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O --(dil. HCl / Δ)--> C₆H₁₂O₆ (Glucose) + C₆H₁₂O₆ (Fructose).
On cooling, alcohol is added; glucose crystallizes out first while fructose remains in solution.

board.text: What is peptide bond? How is it formed? Write the name and formula of the reagent used to convert alkylhalide to nitroalkane.
board.answer:
Peptide bond: An amide bond (−CO−NH−) linking two α-amino acids.
Formation: Formed by condensation of the −COOH group of one α-amino acid with the −NH₂ group of another α-amino acid with elimination of a water molecule.
Reagent for R-X → R-NO₂: Silver nitrite (AgNO₂).

points.text: Condensation of −COOH and −NH₂ with loss of H₂O

board.text: The linkage present in Lactose is ____.
Write classification of proteins with an example.
board.answer:
1. Fibrous proteins: Insoluble in water, thread-like molecules held by H-bonds/disulphide bonds. Example: Keratin (hair, nails) or Myosin (muscles).
2. Globular proteins: Soluble in water, spherical/folded polypeptide chains. Example: Insulin or Haemoglobin / Albumin.
